# Paravoxia — orchestration & token discipline

Fable weekly limits are the binding constraint; most spend is long-context
cache reads, not output. Every session in this repo follows these rules.

## Model tiering (frontmatter already set — don't override upward casually)

- **fable (inherit)**: `chapter-director`, `score-director`,
  `cinematography-director`, `story-alignment-judge`,
  `scene-cohesion-judge` — creative build and taste-critical judgment only.
- **opus**: `story-naive-reader`, `story-canon-auditor`, `story-verifier`,
  `scene-naive-viewer`, `cinematography-continuity-auditor`,
  `score-continuity-auditor`, `player-experience-auditor` — blind reading,
  auditing, and mechanical verification.
- Any ad-hoc Explore/general-purpose agent for searching, doc-reading, log
  triage, or probe-running: pass `model: "opus"` (or `"haiku"` for trivial
  greps). A mechanical subagent must never inherit fable.

## Main-session context hygiene

- Stay an orchestrator. Don't pull the design corpus (~65k tokens:
  `PARAVOXIA_PROGRESSION.md`, `PARAVOXIA_CH4_PLAN.md`, `main/STORY.md`) into
  the main context unless doing the creative work directly here — delegate
  reading to a subagent and keep only its conclusions.
- Verification (movie probes, screenshot strips, `npm run verify`) goes to
  `story-verifier`, not inline Bash loops. Run dev servers and long probes in
  the background; read back tails, never full logs.
- Guided-play changes require both the verifier's objective/marker/feedback
  lifecycle proof and a fresh read-only `player-experience-auditor` report.
  Neither role patches or substitutes for a creative director.
- After finishing a chapter or review, remind the owner to `/clear` before the
  next task; suggest `/compact` before starting a long build phase when
  context is already large.

## This machine runs concurrent sessions

Other agents and the owner work in this repo at the same time. Two incidents in
one session on 2026-09-04:

- A parallel refactor of `main/src/utils/fauna*.ts` landed mid-`verify` and made
  it fail on files the running session had never touched. **Before treating a
  gate failure as yours, check `ls -l` timestamps against your last edit.** Do
  not "fix" a module someone is actively splitting — you will collide with work
  whose destination only they know.
- A probe pointed at `127.0.0.1:5199` measured a DIFFERENT PROJECT after that
  port was taken over. It returned 200 and rendered a real app, so nothing
  looked wrong. **Probes must verify identity, not liveness** — check for
  `<title>Paravoxia</title>` before trusting a measurement. `npm run
  verify:visual` picks a free port and does this check; copy that pattern.

`npm run dev` fails here with `ENOSPC: System limit for number of file watchers
reached` (the `captures/` tree is enormous). Use `npm run build` plus
`npx vite preview`.

Two more harness traps, both hit on 2026-09-04:

- **A background shell that waits with `until ! pgrep -f "<name>"` waits forever**,
  because the pattern matches the waiting shell's own command line. Use the
  bracket trick — `pgrep -f "[n]ame"` — or run dependent steps sequentially in
  one shell instead of polling.
- **Probes must own their server's lifetime.** Nine orphaned `vite preview`
  processes were left behind by probes that crashed. `tools/lib/previewServer.mjs`
  now kills the child on exit/signal; use it rather than spawning a preview by
  hand. Its `assertHardwareGl` check is also mandatory: without `--use-gl=angle`
  headless Chromium here silently used SwiftShader and a boot profile showed a
  20-second stall that the real GPU never produces.
- **Probe switches** (players never set these): `?worldprep=sync` forces the legacy
  synchronous world generation; `?beatregistry=off` serves the legacy story tables
  instead of beat contracts. Both exist so a baseline and a candidate come from ONE build.
- **Edit-then-measure ordering.** A build started 27 seconds after a source edit
  contains that edit. Capture a baseline BEFORE changing the code path it
  measures, or use the same-build A/B switches (`?worldprep=sync`,
  `?beatregistry=off`) so baseline and candidate come from one build.

## Creative triad

For any new scene, awakening, substantial cutscene recut, or audiovisual
polish pass, invoke the `creative-triad` skill. The Chapter, Score, and
Cinematography directors are peers. They communicate through the run's scene
contract and structured director notes; they do not race edits in shared
timeline files or approve their own implementation.

Chapter, Score, and Cinematography are exactly the three peer creative
directors. Auditors, verifiers, judges, and integration engineers provide
checks, evidence, and repair routing; they never become a fourth creative lane.

Durable contracts live in:

- `PARAVOXIA_CREATIVE_COUNCIL.md`
- `main/CINEMATOGRAPHY.md`
- `main/src/story/ux/README.md` (the executable player-guidance context
  contract for objective, marker, HUD, and feedback lifecycles)
- `docs/architecture/workflow-orchestration/examples/paravoxia-creative-triad.workflow.json`
- `.codex/production-runs/_template/`

## Story scope

Post-arrival story work is **authorized**. The owner lifted the post-arrival
gate on 2026-07-28 (recorded at the top of `PARAVOXIA_DEMO_FOUNDATION_PLAN.md`):
story beyond `ch9-hearth` may be designed, built, and registered, including the
space-station chapter. Do not refuse or defer this work on the basis of an
older freeze — earlier revisions of this file carried one, and it expired.

What still applies:

- **Creative-Triad and registry gates are the remaining barrier** between a new
  chapter and the runtime. Route the work through them; do not route around.
- **Sequencing is owner-directed: do not rush to the station.** Making the
  existing story enjoyable comes first, and the need to leave must emerge from
  play rather than from a new content hook.
- **The demo's release surface is unchanged** — it still stops at
  `ch4-arrival`, and publishing remains a separate decision. Building past it
  is allowed; shipping it in the demo is not implied.
- **Shipped copy and audio remain protected baselines.** Changing a protected
  audio/runtime path is still a contracted change, not an incidental one.
- **"Anchorage" is retired as a name.** The location is the **space station**.

# Interim verification checkpoint — Common Ground (ch13)

**This is an interim failure checkpoint, not final chapter verification.** It is
not a scorecard, not a creative judgement, and not a publication decision.
Machine-readable twin: `verification-lifecycle-interim-report.json`.

- Role: independent story-verifier. **No game source was edited.**
- Contract: scene-v2, sha256 `4dbf722b308b92b170313285854e3c9c2abac853b3407bf3e0f4efccfddff88e`
- Source manifest: `58f275f6130914f878942774fd4b4c6ce74327755c33ae257965a9dbeed40e70`
  — all **96 files independently rehashed, 0 mismatch, 0 missing**
- Preview: root-owned `http://127.0.0.1:43617/`, index sha256
  `1f327268…c05b823a`, bundle `/assets/index-CVcXc2R8.js`
  (`c34f1850…c36fca9d9`), verified to contain the repair identifier
  `railTraversal` and the exact signed marker labels
- Renderer: `ANGLE (NVIDIA Corporation, NVIDIA GB10/PCIe, OpenGL 4.5.0)` —
  **real hardware, headed**, each probe under a non-blocking `flock` on the
  shared heavy lock, released on exit

## Verdict

**FAIL (interim).** The repaired build passes every static gate and the ch13-home
interaction repair genuinely holds — but two blocking runtime defects stop the
chapter before any route traversal can be measured at all.

## What passes

| gate | result |
| --- | --- |
| `npm --prefix main run verify` | **exit 0** — 348 test files, **3026 tests**, build ok |
| `creative:gate --phase implementation` | exit 0 — **1708 checks** |
| `story:ux:check` | exit 0 — 9 files / 94 tests |
| changed-source tests (`commonGround*`, `autopilot`) | exit 0 — 13 files / 212 tests |
| six registry/journey/authority/creative/accept smokes | all exit 0 |

Static and CPU only. It proves nothing about rendering, traversal, hearing,
hardware or the movie bridge — and both blockers below are invisible to it.

**CG-IMPL-004 is not reproducible.** On hardware, `ch13:home:review` entered at
7 ms with the exact signed label and work order, was performed through the
**shared** performer (`interactionTrace` source `resolver-perform`, outcome
`returned`, prompt cleared in 0 ms), `ch13:home:choose-return` followed at
2165 ms, and the beat advanced at 2777 ms — 0 nudges, 0 page errors. The
pre-repair capture sat on that same objective for the full 300 s.

Also confirmed: every objective observed carried its **exact** signed marker
label and work order, including the scene-v2 *preparation* conditional copy for
`ch13:common:reciprocal` verbatim; and when Terra's body was 0.38 units from
W-7744 he **held** rather than displacing her (0 teleports), consistent with the
signed rule — observed in a synthetic state, so an observation, not proof.

## Blocker 1 — VF-DEEPLINK-1: the chapter boots aboard the ship

`?story=ch13-survey&movie=1` boots the player **inside the landed Kestrel** and
can never recover. 243.2 s of exactly zero displacement: body frozen at
`[8, 53.85, -6]`, `walkedPathUnits 0.000` over 2237 samples, W-7744 mounted 44 m
away, `spaceFlight {phase:'surface', controlMode:'flight'}` in **every** sample
(the module default is `fps`). The rail is alive and asking correctly
(`routeAction 'walk'`, clock 3.1 → 238.3 s) — on-foot walk simply does nothing in
flight control mode. 0 nudges, 0 page errors, 0 acts attempted.
`post/survey-movie-1/0039-root-checkpoint.png` is shot from inside the cockpit;
the debug HUD reads `Ship: landed`, `Flight: surface / flight`.

Source candidate (read-only): `commonGroundRailPlan()` has an `exit-ship` branch
only under `case 'ch13-return'`; the `ch13-survey` and `ch13-common` cases never
inspect `controlMode`.

## Blocker 2 — VF-RAIL-2: she stands on the mark she cannot reach

With an explicitly labelled disembark fixture applied, the chapter came alive —
`anc.cg.repeated-measure` at 3.3 s, the offer performed,
`anc.cg.demonstration-opened` at 13.8 s, **58.6 real units walked**. Then it
stopped for the remaining ~286 s at `ch13:survey:start`.

| quantity | value |
| --- | --- |
| player body **centre** y | 52.79–52.80 in all 2643 samples |
| authored `CG_POSES.S` | `(-26, 51.05, 12)` |
| min 3D distance, **centre** → S | **1.745** (horizontal 0.13) |
| derived **feet** y (centre − 1.3 − 0.5) | **50.99** — within **0.06** of the authored ground plane |
| distance, **feet** → S | **0.143** |
| rail gate | `CG_RAIL_START_AIM 0.35 + CG_RAIL_ROUTE_ARRIVE 0.35 = 0.70` |
| resolver reach | `CG_POINT_REACH 2.0` — satisfied by 1.745 with 0.255 margin, which is why the prompt shows |
| time standing on the mark | 261 of 354 pose-ledger entries (~4.5 min) |
| live prompt throughout | `F | Begin recording your route` |
| acts performed | **0**, with 0 teleport nudges |

`post/survey-diag-1/0038-strip-ch13-survey.png` shows the marker reading
**`survey start · begin a route · 0m`** with the F prompt on screen.

**Reconciled against the real body, as root asked — and it sharpens rather than
dissolves the finding.** `getPlayerWorldPosition()` returns the Rapier capsule
*centre*; `EfficientPlayer.tsx:1525` itself derives feet as centre − half-height.
Her feet are on the authored plane. The body *has* arrived; only the comparison
frame disagrees. **This is a coordinate-frame (centre-vs-feet / vertical
inclusion) mismatch, not a too-tight radius.** How to reconcile it is the
integrator's decision — widening radii would mask it and could relax genuine
physical clearance rules.

Why 3026 tests miss it: `commonGroundDirector.test.ts:99` `standAt()` places the
world position at the authored pose y — **a body of zero height** — so every rail
regression runs at vertical offset 0. Gates below the live 1.745 offset:
`CG_RAIL_ROUTE_ARRIVE 0.35`, `CG_RAIL_POSE_ARRIVE 0.6` (offer-span at E),
`CG_RAIL_START_AIM+ARRIVE 0.70`, `CG_RAIL_CORNER_OVERSHOOT 0.6`.

## Open anomaly for the same pass — VF-ANCHOR-OBS-1 (revised)

I **withdraw** my earlier inference that all four ch13-home anchors are provable
only in a continuous journey; Score's interpretation rejects that reading and I
accept the correction. Only `anc.cg.cell-installed` needs the live install
boundary. So the fact that deep-linked ch13-home performed both real F acts and
set both milestones while `activationHistoryAnchorIds` stayed empty in-loop is an
**anomaly**, not expected behaviour.

Source candidates, unconfirmed: `noteAnchor()` latches `runtime.firedAnchors`
*before* calling `activateSignedSceneAnchorById` and discards its boolean, so a
rejected activation is spent locally and never retried; and `activateAnchor()`
refuses an anchor while an earlier pending ordered same-beat anchor is
unactivated. Not proven — I did not instrument the return value. **No audibility
claim:** nothing was listened to, and Score rightly notes local score dispatch
may continue despite a rejected AV activation.

Separately, the empty `anchorLedger` in `home-movie-2` is a capture-window
artefact, not missing instrumentation: the loop exited on its `--until-beat`
predicate at 2777 ms and `anc.cg.hatch-boarded` activated after that. Anchor
capture demonstrably works elsewhere.

## What was NOT measured — and is therefore NOT claimed

- **The CG-IMPL-005 ordered-cursor repair in a browser.** No route traversal was
  ever entered. Retarget-to-visited-start, corner shortcuts, the ordered 18
  units, long-vs-short route classes and first-try-legal long success: **all
  unmeasured**.
- **Manual-corner deviation and recovery — not reached.** The
  `commonGroundRoute.ts:444-479` projection risk stays a source/test risk,
  deliberately kept separate from the two measured blockers.
- Three cold focused journeys; both route classes; the continuous
  station→home→ch13 bridge; the full story movie from the beginning.
- The 28 anchors as a set; the 17+2 objective lifecycles end to end; the 8-trigger
  reset matrix; mobile / reduced-motion / lowest-tier; pause / focus / quit /
  deep-link / replay.
- Any performance, fps, draw-call, memory or timing figure.
- Any score, cue, spacing or release behaviour. **Nothing was listened to.**
- The headed `chapter:evidence` bundle for chapter13.
- The typed final artifacts (`verification-report`,
  `objective-lifecycle-evidence`, `chapter-journey-evidence`,
  `raw-audiovisual-evidence`, `evidence-registry`) are **deliberately not
  authored**: filling their schemas now would mean writing booleans without
  measurements.

## Prerequisite fixtures (labelled, and not journey evidence)

`post/survey-diag-1` and `post/common-diag-1` each pressed the shipped ordinary
disembark key once (`KeyF`, `App.tsx:1516-1525`), only because the entry had
booted aboard the ship, recorded with before/after state in
`summary.prerequisiteFixtures`. It grants no milestone, position, progress or
route credit. **Those two runs are diagnostics — not cold journeys, not
continuous proof, and are not reported as either.**

## Integrity

No game source edited. No threshold or predicate changed. No teleport, progress
grant or timeout-as-rescue anywhere. No unrun check marked passed. No creative
judgement offered. Pre-repair captures and `verifier/logs/verify.log` preserved
untouched; all new evidence lives under `verifier/captures/post/` and
`verifier/logs/post-repair/`. No server was started or orphaned by this role; the
root-owned preview at `http://127.0.0.1:43617/` is root's and remains running.

Raw media inventories with per-file sha256 are in the JSON twin, kept separate
from this prose so a blind viewer can receive only the media.

# Manual corner interpretation — Chapter

contractVersion: `scene-v2`  
contractSha256: `4dbf722b308b92b170313285854e3c9c2abac853b3407bf3e0f4efccfddff88e`  
contractChangeRequired: **false for a bounded implementation correction meeting the conditions below**  
authoredAt: 2026-09-06T09:47:14.579038+00:00

The signed intent allows ordinary small manual deviations and honest recovery. It requires the real ordered eighteen-unit passage, not frame-perfect coincidence with mathematical corner coordinates. It does not bind `routeProgressUnits`' current projection algorithm or promise credit for omitted ground. A deviation may leave part of the route unproved; the player must be able to resume its actual traversal through ordinary movement, without a hidden precision ritual, reset, additional F or new corner prompts.

This is an interpretation of source and recorded engineering evidence, **not an independently observed manual failure**. `producer-manual-corner-risk.json` records the director test turning at z15.82 before z16 and stalling at four credited units; it also records the corrected movie controller completing its actual eighteen-unit test. Browser/manual acceptance remains pending. In `main/src/story/commonGroundRoute.ts:444–479`, each accepted arc projection must fit `previousUnits + displacementUnits` for that frame; later projections can stay beyond that ceiling after an early turn. The source supports the reported risk but does not establish its frequency or the usability of recovery in play.

The relevant exact signed clauses are:

- `scene-contract.json#/guidance/objectives/13/acceptanceCriterion`: full actual eighteen-unit E→C passage, and first-time manual success without private route knowledge, a rail or per-corner prompts.
- `#/story/agencyWindows/3/mandatoryPath`: the complete guided common route and both real reciprocal traversals; positioning earns no proof. Its `fallbackSemantics` requires a safe hold and actionable objective when a predicate is unmet, while `rescueSemantics` forbids granting progress to escape a stall.
- `#/story/events/21/acceptanceCriterion`: current H reference, solid sight, grounding and clearance throughout; endpoint separation, old footsteps, saved proof and elapsed time cannot substitute. The matching `#/syncAnchors/21/acceptanceCriterion` binds the same event.

If independent verification confirms the risk, a bounded correction must let genuinely performed ordered traversal resume from retained valid progress and reach actual C while still proving the **full actual eighteen units**, maintained reference, supported movement, body clearance and physical arrival. It must neither discard earned progress because of a small steering error nor credit the missing portion merely because the body reached a later segment. Stationary time, looping elsewhere, endpoint proximity, skipped bends, accumulated unrelated distance and automatic rescue remain insufficient. Restore must preserve earned facts and revalidate current physical conditions.

That outcome implements existing v2 agency and proof requirements; it needs no contract amendment. A proposal that shortens the passage, skips order or physical checks, changes route geometry, adds a required input/target, or manufactures credit would exceed this interpretation and require separate routing. No algorithm, tolerance, source patch or new repair authorization is prescribed here. Root retains repair routing; independent manual and Continue proof remains necessary even though the movie test passes.
=====SCORE=====
# Score interpretation — home-anchor eligibility

**Later eligible home anchors must remain usable on Continue or a valid deep link while the ineligible live install acknowledgement stays silent.** Suppressing the entire home-anchor sequence is not an interpretation of the signed hydration rule. This is a bounded interpretation of scene-v2, not a new direction, independent runtime acceptance or authorization to fabricate receipts.

Contract: `scene-contract.json`, SHA-256 **`4dbf722b308b92b170313285854e3c9c2abac853b3407bf3e0f4efccfddff88e`**. Reviewed `verifier-findings.json#VF-ANCHOR-OBS-1`, its home/survey summary artifacts, and the requested source owners.

## Binding clauses

- `/syncAnchors/0` (`anc.cg.cell-installed`) requires the **actual live install receipt**, one consumed cell and at most one acknowledgement when a home score host is available. Its acceptance explicitly says a hydrated entry is steady and silent, consuming no second cell. `/score/cues/0` likewise permits no completion transient on restore and no listening gate.
- `/syncAnchors/1` (`anc.cg.home-steady`) explicitly restores the steady home variant on hydrated entry, without a completion transient or queued acknowledgement. Its real departed/restored receipts, on-foot Tidegarden and actual-core conditions remain required.
- `/guidance/objectives/0` enters at home-steady and states that **a restored save reaches the review objective without replaying the transaction**. Its entry feedback is silent on hydration. The invitation therefore remains functional independently of fresh install presentation.
- `/syncAnchors/2` and `/syncAnchors/3` bind fault-reviewed to the actual core interaction and return-chosen to the explicit F commit. The latter releases the home quotation; fault review does not change it. `/guidance/objectives/1` preserves that voluntary choice. None of these clauses requires another installation.

## Required invariant and evidence distinction

Eligibility, actual activation and audible acknowledgement are distinct. A restored transaction must not be represented as a fresh installation to satisfy ordering. Equally, its ineligible live acknowledgement must not become a permanently pending prerequisite for silent steady entry or subsequent real F actions. Already-earned review/choice state restores without falsely replaying its action; a new eligible interaction retains its signed anchor. No missing receipt, core, actor/world condition or player action may be supplied by this interpretation. Return-chosen still releases home score through the existing authority; travel remains with the world conductor.

The verifier's summaries support an observed separation: the home run reached real review/return progression with an empty home anchor ledger, while the survey run recorded repeated-measure. The home loop stopped at the return-beat predicate at 2777 ms; its later hatch anchor is a separate capture-window issue. Those observations do not justify VF-ANCHOR-OBS-1's conclusion that **all four** home anchors should be observable only during a continuous journey. Only the fresh install event requires that live boundary. The evidence does not itself prove an audible failure: local score dispatch can continue despite rejected AV activation, and no listening occurred here.

Source risk: `noteAnchor` records its local once-latch before calling AV activation and does not consume its returned success value. `activateAnchor` rejects later anchors while an earlier required same-beat anchor remains pending. `enterCommonGroundBeat` requests home-steady on entry, while `tickCommonGroundEntry` calls reactivation before requesting cell-installed. If entry callbacks run before that latter request, the live path can also reject and locally spend home-steady before installation activates. This is an entry-order/latch risk requiring continuous-path evidence, **not an observed continuous-journey failure**.

## Amendment disposition

Role: single integration engineer. Contract scene-v2
`4dbf722b308b92b170313285854e3c9c2abac853b3407bf3e0f4efccfddff88e` (preserved,
not re-signed). Direction: `lifecycle-repair-direction.json` (CG-IMPL-006/007/008)
plus the recorded manual-corner risk. No publication, no browser/GPU in this role.

## Phase 0 — boundary and preservation (done)

- Read `production-lock.json` (allowedPaths / protectedPaths / bounded-runtime),
  `scene-contract.json` signatures + `contract-gate-pass.json`,
  `lifecycle-repair-direction.json`, `repair-contract-disposition.json`,
  `verification-lifecycle-interim-report.{json,md}`, `verifier-findings.json`,
  `chapter-manual-corner-interpretation.md`,

  `producer-manual-corner-risk.json`, `integration-inbox.md` (tail).
- Rehashed the exact 96-file `implementation-source-manifest.json`:
  **96/96 identical, 0 drift, 0 missing.** Source is the frozen state the
  verifier measured; the initial dirty tree is preserved.
- Verifier invocation finished 10:23:03Z; no other writer is running.

## Phase 1 — causal diagnosis (done, source-read only)

### CG-IMPL-007 / VF-DEEPLINK-1 — boot causal owner FOUND
`main/src/story/storyState.ts#initStoryFromSave` seeds `?story=ch13-survey` and
`?story=ch13-common` with `bootstrapOriginLaunchDebug()`. That helper ends in
`restoreBoardedSurfaceFlight()` (`spaceFlight.ts:431`) → `{phase:'surface',
controlMode:'flight'}` — i.e. **seated in the landed Kestrel**, which is the
correct ch8-launch/ch10-transit staging and the wrong one for two on-foot beats.
It is the *seeding* owner, not `commonGroundRailPlan`: the rail's missing
`exit-ship` branch is a downstream inability to recover, not the cause.
Continue/continuous return already agree with on-foot (`restoreFlightAtLocation`
does not transfer cockpit ownership; ch13-return performs a real disembark).

### CG-IMPL-006 / VF-RAIL-2 — one coordinate frame, whole chapter
`commonGroundDirector.player()` returns `getPlayerWorldPosition()` raw. That is
the **Rapier capsule centre** (`CapsuleCollider [half 1.3, radius 0.5]`,
`EfficientPlayer.tsx:2078`); the chapter's authored poses are grounded body
origins at y 51.05. The offset is `HALF_HEIGHT + RADIUS = 1.8` along the live
local up. Consequences found beyond the rail gate the verifier measured:
- `CommonGroundWorld.createFooting` reads `cell(y - 1.05)`; a centre at 52.79
  samples the EMPTY cell above the ground column, so `isSupported` is false —
  `commitCommonGroundSurveyStart`, trace sampling, witness offers and the final
  reference offer are all unreachable, not only the rail's 0.35/0.70 gates.
- `walkToward` measures `surfaceGaitDistance` (tangential + unclimbed rise;
  `GAIT_STEP_DOWN 3.4` swallows the 1.8 drop), so the shared walker stops on
  HORIZONTAL distance while the director judged full 3D from 1.8 above. The two
  frames disagreed by exactly the capsule.
Fix direction: convert once, at the director's `player()` boundary, using the
real constants and `getPlayerUp()`; every downstream predicate (recording,
supported ground, sockets, occupancy, clearance, arrival, progress) then reads
the pose semantics it was authored for. No radius widening, no y-clamp, no
disabled vertical check.

### CG-IMPL-008 — two distinct wiring faults, plus a latent third
1. Ordering: `signedSceneAvRuntime.activateAnchor` treats every ch13 anchor as a
   mandatory ordered prerequisite. `anc.cg.cell-installed` (order 0) is signed as
   the LIVE install receipt and cannot exist on a hydrated/deep-linked entry, so
   home-steady/fault-reviewed/return-chosen are refused forever.
2. Latch: `noteAnchor` adds to `runtime.firedAnchors` BEFORE calling
   `activateSignedSceneAnchorById` and discards its boolean, so a refusal is
   spent locally and never retried.
3. Live-path order: `tickCommonGroundEntry` calls `reactivateStoryAtBeat` (which
   re-enters the beat and immediately requests home-steady, order 1) BEFORE
   requesting cell-installed (order 0) — so the one live acknowledgement is
   rejected by the monotonic guard on the live path too.
Latent (same root, downstream of the measured one): the seven signed
`Contingent:` anchors are also treated as prerequisites, which would refuse
`anc.cg.route-tested` and `anc.cg.complete` whenever a contingency did not occur.

### Manual corner (recorded risk) — reproduction pending in phase 2

## Phase 2 — implementation (in progress)

/**
 * Capsule centre -> grounded body origin, in the walker's own gravity frame.
 *
 * THE ONE COORDINATE SEAM OF THIS CHAPTER, and it is a physical fact rather than
 * a tolerance. `getPlayerWorldPosition()` publishes the Rapier body's origin,
 * which is the CENTRE of the capsule collider `EfficientPlayer` mounts
 * (`CapsuleCollider [PLAYER_CAPSULE_HALF_HEIGHT, PLAYER_CAPSULE_RADIUS]`). Every
 * pose this chapter was authored against — `CG_POSES`, the three routes, the
 * sockets, the occupancy cylinders, the footing columns — is a GROUNDED body
 * origin: the point the feet contact. The two differ by the half-height plus the
 * lower cap radius, along the LOCAL up, because this is a cube-gravity world and
 * "down" is not `-Y` on five of its six faces.
 *
 * Reading the raw centre was wrong everywhere, not merely at the rail's arrival
 * radius: `CommonGroundWorld`'s footing samples `cell(y - 1.05)`, so a centre
 * 1.8 above the ground column samples the EMPTY cell above it and reports
 * unsupported — which silently refused the survey start, every trace sample,
 * every witness offer and the far-reference offer. The shared walker
 * (`surfaceGaitDistance`) meanwhile measures tangential range, so it stopped on
 * horizontal distance while this module judged full 3D from 1.8 units up. One
 * conversion here makes the walker, the terrain and the contract agree.
 *
 * NOTHING IS WIDENED, CLAMPED OR SKIPPED. The vertical term stays in every
 * comparison, so a jumping or floating body is still not standing anywhere: it
 * is simply measured from where her feet actually are.
 */
export const CG_PLAYER_GROUND_OFFSET = PLAYER_CAPSULE_HALF_HEIGHT + PLAYER_CAPSULE_RADIUS;

/**
 * Where the player's feet ACTUALLY are, this frame.
 *
 * Exported for the physical regressions, which must place a capsule centre and
 * assert against the ground plane rather than standing a body of zero height on
 * the mark.
 */
export function commonGroundPlayerPose(): CommonGroundPoint {
  const position = getPlayerWorldPosition();
  const up = getPlayerUp();
  return {
    x: position.x - up.x * CG_PLAYER_GROUND_OFFSET,
    y: position.y - up.y * CG_PLAYER_GROUND_OFFSET,
    z: position.z - up.z * CG_PLAYER_GROUND_OFFSET
  };
}

function player(): CommonGroundPoint {
  return commonGroundPlayerPose();
}

function isOptionalAnchor(anchor: SignedAnchor): boolean {
  return anchor.event.endsWith(':optional')
    || RELOCATED_OPTIONAL_ANCHORS.has(anchor.id);
}

/**
 * Signed anchors that MAY NOT HAPPEN, and therefore cannot be prerequisites.
 *
 * Ordering is the invariant that makes a physical transaction inspectable, and
 * none of it is removed here: an anchor listed below still has its signed order,
 * still cannot rewind an already newer shot, and still fires only from its real
 * producer. What is corrected is a category error — treating an event the
 * contract itself declares conditional as a gate every LATER event must wait
 * behind. When the condition does not occur, the rest of the beat is refused
 * forever, and the local producer spends its one-shot latch on the refusal.
 *
 * Each id is here because the signed scene-v2 contract says so, in these words:
 *
 *   `anc.cg.cell-installed` — "/syncAnchors/0" is "the actual live install
 *     receipt from the prior station-continuation contract", and its acceptance
 *     criterion states that "a hydrated entry is steady and silent and consumes
 *     no second cell". A restored save or a valid deep link therefore CANNOT
 *     produce it, while "/syncAnchors/1" (home-steady) must still "restore the
 *     steady home variant on hydrated entry" and "/guidance/objectives/0" must
 *     still reach the review objective "without replaying the transaction".
 *     Measured (VF-ANCHOR-OBS-1): a hydrated ch13-home performed both real F
 *     acts and set both milestones while no home anchor ever activated.
 *
 *   `anc.cg.revision-ready` and the eight anchors whose signed event text begins
 *     "Contingent:" — "/syncAnchors/12" says "No refusal is required, no F has
 *     committed yet ... A valid current route may remain unchanged";
 *     "/syncAnchors/13" says "any supported route, including the measured long
 *     route, may complete without this anchor. Do not force failure"; and
 *     "/syncAnchors/19" says "first-try success is legal". A first-try legal
 *     route would otherwise never reach route-tested, and a common span walked
 *     without a reference lapse would never reach `anc.cg.complete`.
 *
 * `signedSceneAvRuntime.test.ts` asserts this set against the compiled contract
 * so a future anchor cannot drift out of it silently.
 */
const CONDITIONAL_ANCHORS: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set([
  'anc.cg.cell-installed',
  'anc.cg.revision-ready',
  'anc.cg.specific-hold',
  'anc.cg.witness-held',
  'anc.cg.witness-vacated',
  'anc.cg.test-resumed',
  'anc.cg.tail-reopened',
  'anc.cg.route-revised',
  'anc.cg.reference-vacated',
  'anc.cg.reference-resumed'
]);

/** True when the contract declares this anchor conditional rather than required. */
export function isConditionalSignedAnchor(anchorId: string): boolean {
  return CONDITIONAL_ANCHORS.has(anchorId);
}

"""Byte-exact counterfactual harness.

Saves the CURRENT bytes of each file, applies a mutation, runs a command, and
restores from those private bytes in a finally block, rehashing to prove the
restore. Never touches Git: this tree is deliberately dirty.
"""
import hashlib
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path


def sha(path: Path) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def run_counterfactual(edits, command, cwd):
    saved = {}
    for path in edits:
        p = Path(path)
        saved[p] = (p.read_bytes(), sha(p))
    try:
        for path, mutate in edits.items():
            p = Path(path)
            p.write_text(mutate(p.read_text()))
        proc = subprocess.run(command, cwd=cwd, capture_output=True, text=True)
        return proc
    finally:
        restored = []
        for p, (data, before) in saved.items():
            p.write_bytes(data)
            after = sha(p)
            assert after == before, f'restore mismatch for {p}: {before} != {after}'
            restored.append((str(p), after))
        for path, digest in restored:
            print(f'restored {path} {digest}', file=sys.stderr)
PY

# Integration lifecycle repair — Common Ground (ch13)

Machine-readable twin: `integration-lifecycle-repair-report.json`. Diff:
`lifecycle-repair.diff`. Logs: `evidence/integration-lifecycle-repair/`.

- Role: the single integration engineer. **No browser, no GPU, no `npm run
  verify`, nothing rendered and nothing listened to.**
- Contract: scene-v2 `4dbf722b…fddff88e`, unchanged and re-signed by nobody.
- Direction: `lifecycle-repair-direction.json` — CG-IMPL-006/007/008 plus a
  reproduction of the recorded manual-corner risk.
- Starting source: the exact 96-file manifest, rehashed independently before any
  edit — **96/96 identical, 0 drift, 0 missing.**
- Result: `npm run test` **3062 passed** (baseline 3026, +36, −0), typecheck,
  build and eleven static gates all exit 0; `creative:gate --phase
  implementation` passes with 1708 checks.

**This proves no gameplay.** Every claim below is a source and test claim.

## CG-IMPL-007 — the chapter booted aboard the ship

**Cause, at the actual owner.** `storyState.initStoryFromSave` seeds
`?story=ch13-survey` and `?story=ch13-common` with
`bootstrapOriginLaunchDebug()`, whose last statement is
`restoreBoardedSurfaceFlight()` → `{phase:'surface', controlMode:'flight'}`.
That is exactly right for `ch8-launch` and `ch10-transit`, which *begin in the
cockpit*, and exactly wrong for two beats that begin after ch13-return has
already landed and disembarked. On-foot walk input does nothing in flight

## Fourth pass — the lifecycle repair (CG-IMPL-006/007/008)

Full detail: `integration-lifecycle-repair-report.{json,md}`, diff
`lifecycle-repair.diff`, logs `evidence/integration-lifecycle-repair/`. The
independent verifier's interim failure checkpoint on the frozen source is the
evidence this pass answers; root routed it in `lifecycle-repair-direction.json`.
The 96-file manifest was rehashed before the first edit: **96/96 identical.**

**The chapter booted aboard the ship (CG-IMPL-007).** The causal owner is
`storyState.initStoryFromSave`, which seeds `?story=ch13-survey` and
`?story=ch13-common` with `bootstrapOriginLaunchDebug()` — whose last statement
restores *boarded* surface flight. That is right for the beats that begin in the
cockpit and wrong for two beats that begin after ch13-return has landed and
disembarked, and on-foot walk input does nothing in flight control mode. Both
now seed on foot through the shipped `restoreFlightAtLocation('surface')`: no
exit receipt, no listener, no milestone, and the landed Kestrel stays parked.
The screening rail can also leave a landed ship inside those two beats rather
than stalling — never a per-frame auto-disembark, and `ch13-return` is asserted
unchanged.

**The chapter was measuring a body of zero height (CG-IMPL-006).** `player()`
returned the raw Rapier capsule *centre*; every authored pose is a *grounded*
body origin, 1.8 units below it along the live local up. The damage was wider
than the arrival gate the verifier measured: the mounted world's footing samples
the cell under `y − 1.05`, so a centre 1.8 up sampled the **empty** cell and
reported unsupported — silently refusing the survey start, every trace sample,
both reference offers — while the shared walker stopped on *tangential* gait
distance. One conversion at the chapter boundary, from the real capsule
constants and `getPlayerUp()`, now feeds recording, supported ground, sockets,
occupancy, clearance, arrival and progress alike. **No radius widened, no
vertical term dropped, no `y` clamped, no ground faked, no protected file
edited.** `standAt()` now places a real capsule centre and the rail harness uses
the real `surfaceGaitDistance`; with the fix reverted, **24 previously passing
tests fail**, which is precisely why 3026 tests could not see it.

**The home anchors could never activate (CG-IMPL-008).** The signed live-install
receipt was treated as a mandatory prerequisite for the whole beat, the eight
signed *Contingent* anchors likewise for `route-tested` and `complete`; the
director latched an anchor before asking and discarded the answer; and the
shared director enters this chapter's seam one call *before* the AV rail, so the
entry anchor was always refused. Conditional anchors are now exempt from being
prerequisites (with contract citations and a drift guard — the order guard,
one-shot latch and required chain all stand), a refusal is retried exactly once
on the next frame of the same beat and dropped otherwise, and the install
receipt is published before the steady entry it causes. Every anchor regression
drives the real `signedSceneAvRuntime`, never a spy.

**The manual-corner risk: reproduced, and deliberately not "fixed".** At walking
pace, turning 0.18 units early credits 4.000 of 18 for 17.83 walked. But it is a
lock only for a body that never goes back: returning to the frontier it reached
and re-traversing credits **exactly 18.0000**, with earned progress retained, no
reset, no second `F` and no new marker — while a far-end wiggle and a 30-unit
unrelated loop credit nothing. A frontier-creep reconciliation was built,
measured and **removed**, because it pays for omitted ground with in-corridor
distance, which the Chapter interpretation forbids. `commonGroundRoute.ts`
therefore differs in comments only. The remaining question — whether ~48 walked
units for an 18-unit span after a 0.18-unit slip is acceptable — is creative, and
is routed to root and Chapter rather than decided here.

**Observability.** `window.__paravoxiaCommonGround.snapshot()`, installed by
`StoryDirectorDriver.tsx` only under `?journeyprobe=1`/`?chapterjourney=1`/
`?debug=1`, returns copies of the beat, the capsule centre, the grounded pose,
